extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners submitting entries to the PRSA Anvil Awards (in-house communications teams, PR agencies, vendors, college/university programs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation criteria for submitting work to the 2025 PRSA Anvil Awards, including category definitions, submission requirements, judging criteria for Silver (strategic/organizational) and Bronze (tactical) awards, and supporting-materials rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil Strategic Campaign Awards — general standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Silver Anvil Awards celebrate the best strategic communications campaigns of the year and must meet the highest standards of performance in the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-Page Summary is the single-most important component for Silver Strategic Campaign entries; entries are judged on insights & analysis, planning, execution and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil Tactical Awards — general standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Bronze Anvil Awards recognize outstanding communications tactics that contribute to the success of overall programs or campaigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-Page Summary is the single-most important component for Bronze Tactical entries; judges evaluate planning/content, creativity/quality, technical excellence (except media relations), and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging outcome rules (winners/runners-up/finalists)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges will select only one Anvil, and up to three runners-up in each category/subcategory; if judges determine there is no winner, there will be no runner-up awards in that category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalists will be notified by end of March 2025 and winners announced in May 2025 at the ceremony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility period
rubrics_metrics.description: At least some part of the work must have occurred during Feb 1, 2023 – Feb 1, 2025; the program must have been initiated no earlier than Jan 1, 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple category submissions rule
rubrics_metrics.description: An entry may be submitted in multiple categories, provided it applies to the specific criteria stated within each category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants can copy a submission via the 'Copy Submission' link on the Review and Checkout page. Judges will not move entries to better-suited categories — entrants must select appropriate categories themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic entry information required
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants must select category, provide unique title, name of organization/client, agency name (if any), and a 100-word description of the program/submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each title must be unique or it will be renamed by the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image file requirements for entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload up to three graphic images representative of your program for use on-screen and in publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable file formats: jpg, tif, eps, native Illustrator, Photoshop or hi-res pdf. Artwork should generally be at least 1,000 pixels in width or height.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit in English. Entries produced in a language other than English must be translated prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics compliance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: By entering, entrants confirm programs/entries comply with PRSA Code of Ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an entry has an aspect of 'ethics performance' that's instructive/vital, include commentary of no more than four sentences. PRSA may take action if it becomes aware of non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: All entries must be submitted online
rubrics_metrics.description: All entries and entry materials must be submitted online through PRSA's submission system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entries become PRSA property and fees non-refundable
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries become the property of PRSA. All entry fees are non-refundable. Judges' decisions are final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver — Two-Page Summary requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A two-page PDF summary is the single-most important component of a Silver Anvil Strategic Campaign entry and should begin with a brief situation analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary must address the four entry criteria: insights & analysis, planning, execution, and evaluation. Supporting materials referenced must be uploaded as separate PDFs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver — Supporting materials upload limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants will upload four separate PDFs of any detailed supporting materials referenced in the two-page summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each supporting-PDF: no more than 225 pages and maximum file size 10MB.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF upload formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Uploaded documents must be PDFs with pages no larger than 8.5 x 11 inches (A4 for international entries), minimum 10-point typeface and one-inch margins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver — Judging criteria (four core dimensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anvil Judges evaluate Silver entries on four criteria: insights and analysis, planning, execution and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should begin with a brief situation analysis. Visit the PRSA archive of winning case studies for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insights and analysis (Silver criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: What methods/strategies/tools were implemented to arrive at insights and analysis? Specify primary and/or secondary research used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary research examples: focus groups, interviews, data/analytics software, surveys. Secondary research examples: database searches, web research, industry reports, internal analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning (Silver criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the plan correlated to insights, the general plan, specific measurable objectives, target audiences, overall strategy, and budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about objectives and how the planning derived from insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution (Silver criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the plan was executed and outcomes; include activity flow, key tactics, difficulties encountered and mitigation, partner organizations, and use of nontraditional PR tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless entering under 'Integrated Communications', advertising costs should not exceed one-third of the budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation (Silver criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify methods of evaluation, results, comparison to measurable objectives from planning, and how results reflect original strategy and planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide qualitative and/or quantitative evidence linking results to objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising-costs limit (general guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Silver entries (and general guidance), advertising costs should not exceed one-third of the budget unless the entry is in Integrated Communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting materials relevance warning
rubrics_metrics.description: Absence of relevant and meaningful supporting materials will result in significantly lower scores and can effectively eliminate the entry from consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure supporting PDFs thoroughly support the four Silver criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most Effective Campaign budget categories — staff time/overhead exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget-based categories (Most Effective Campaign on $5,000–$10,000 and Shoestrring $5,000 or less) exclude staff time and overhead from the budget calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 1. Community Relations (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs that aim to improve relations with, or win the support/cooperation of, people or organizations in communities where the sponsor has interest, need or opportunity; 'community' refers to a specific geographic location(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories: 1A Associations/Nonprofit, 1B Government, 1C Business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 2. Content Marketing (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs that effectively demonstrate a strategic program that includes creating and distributing valuable content to attract, acquire, and engage target audience(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include examples and metrics to show effectiveness. Subcategories: 2A Associations/Govt/Nonprofit, 2B B2B, 2C B2C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 3. Crisis Communications (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs undertaken to deal with an unplanned event that required an immediate response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 4. Events and Observances (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes virtual or in-person programs/events like commemorations, conferences, openings, anniversaries, celebrations or other special activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories split by duration: 4A More Than Seven Days (4AA Associations/Govt/Nonprofit; 4AB Business) and 4B Seven Or Fewer Days (4BA Associations/Govt/Nonprofit; 4BB Business). Events longer than one week go in 4A; events within one week in 4B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 5. Financial Communications (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs directed to shareholders, other investors and the investment community; includes communication programs related to decentralized currencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 6. Global Communications (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes any type of program (e.g., Reputation/Brand Management, Marketing, Events) that demonstrates effective global communications implemented in more than one country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 7. Influencer Marketing (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs using influencers; has subcategories for Macro-Influencers and Micro-Influencers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Macro-influencers defined as 10,000–1M followers (celebrities, execs, bloggers, journalists) and have high topical relevance. Micro-influencers defined as 500–10,000 followers (everyday consumers, employees, industry experts) with high brand relevance/resonance driven by personal experience/relationship strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 8. Integrated Communications (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes creative and effective integrated campaigns that combine paid, earned, shared and owned efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate the meaningful PR/communications components and how they integrated with other disciplines. Subcategories: 8A Associations/Nonprofit, 8B Government, 8C B2B, 8D Consumer Products, 8E Consumer Services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 9. Internal Communications (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs targeted specifically to special publics directly allied with an organization (employees, members, affiliated dealers, franchisees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories: 9A Associations/Govt/Nonprofit, 9B Business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 10. Issues Management (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: For programs undertaken to deal with issues that could extraordinarily affect ongoing business strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 11. Marketing (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs designed to introduce new products/services or promote existing products/services to a particular audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories: 11A B2B, 11B Consumer Products – Regional Focus, 11C Consumer Products – National/International Focus, 11D Consumer Services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 12. Most Effective Campaign on a $5,000 to $10,000 Budget (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes an effective campaign delivered within the parameters of a limited budget ($5,000–$10,000), excluding staff time and overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 13. Most Effective Campaign on a Shoestring Budget ($5,000 or less) (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes successful campaigns despite constraints of a very small budget (≤ $5,000), excluding staff time and overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 14. Most Effective Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) Campaign (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts devoted to promoting inclusivity and/or dismantling discrimination for racial, ethnic, religious, sexual orientation and gender differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 15. Climate Action & Environmental Sustainability (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors excellence in energy efficiency, natural resources, programs and campaigns that limit greenhouse gas emissions, minimize waste and contamination, protect/restore ecosystems, and contribute to adaptation to climate change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 16. Corporate Citizenship (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrates campaigns/programs that ignite individuals, technology, and partnerships to create positive societal impact locally, nationally or internationally (poverty, hunger, housing, health, climate, equity, education, human rights, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 17. Multicultural Public Relations (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any type of program (institutional, marketing, community relations) specifically targeted to a cultural group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 18. Public Affairs (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs specifically designed to influence public policy and/or affect legislation, regulations, political activities or candidacies at local, state or federal levels so that the funding entity benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 19. Public Service (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs that advance public understanding of societal issues, problems or concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories: 19A Associations/Government/Nonprofit Organizations, 19B Business, 19C Partnerships (funded jointly by businesses and other organizations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: 20. Reputation/Brand Management (Silver Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs designed to enhance, promote or improve the reputation of an organization with its publics or key elements of its publics, proactively or in response to an issue/event/market occurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories: 20A Associations/Govt/Nonprofit, 20B Business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best of Silver Anvil selection standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A Best of Silver Anvil Award is selected from among the year’s Silver Anvil Strategic Campaign Award winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents the pinnacle of excellence in PR programming and demonstrates PR's strategic value and ability to drive critical business outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Organizational Awards — general standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational awards honor teams/organizations that demonstrate excellence in public relations or innovative programs and measurable impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different organizational awards have distinct required supporting materials and criteria (see individual award entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Award: 1. Best In-House Team
rubrics_metrics.description: A PR/public affairs/communications team that demonstrates excellence in public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission requirements: Two-page summary describing organization and outstanding accomplishments/strategic benchmarks; differentiate role of in-house team vs external resources; include measurable impact, challenges handled, innovation, influence on behavior/attitudes, culture. Upload two brief case studies (≤500 words each) or current Silver Anvil submissions; include number of employees and annual PR budget (including staffing costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Award: 2. Best Agency
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency team that demonstrates excellence in public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission: Two-page summary of agency and accomplishments; two brief case studies (≤500 words each) or current Silver submissions; include number of employees, annual revenue, and a one-page PDF client list from past 12 months including tenure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Award: 3. Best Solution Provider/Vendor
rubrics_metrics.description: A PR/comms solution provider/vendor that demonstrates how its tool/platform is best-in-class and the meaningful impacts delivered for clients and industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission: Two-page summary describing how services are first-in-class and tailored to support communications industry; letters of recommendation — two from customers/clients supporting the submission. Subcategories include Media Monitoring, AI-Automation Resource, Media Database and Intelligence, Analytics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Award: 4. Organization With the Most Impactful DEI Program
rubrics_metrics.description: A team focused on shaping and implementing effective DEI initiatives that have created a more supportive/rewarding working environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission: Two-page summary of team leading efforts and detailed description of programs/practices/initiatives, examples of resources or internal programming, how efforts advance DEI externally, and future plans. Upload two brief case studies (≤500 words each) or current Anvil submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Award: 5. Best College/University Communications Program/Department
rubrics_metrics.description: A college/university team that best prepares the next generation of communication practitioners through innovative curriculum and high standards for student success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission: Two-page summary including job-readiness evidence and metrics (admissions, graduation trends, employment, internship placement); upload two brief case studies (≤500 words each) or current Silver submissions. Requirements: Institution must have PRSSA chapter and hold a Certificate in Education for Academic Programs in Public Relations (CEPR). Provide number of educators (full-time/part-time/adjunct) and faculty's PRSA involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Award: 6. Best AI Integration and Digital Innovations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes exceptional creativity, effectiveness and ingenuity in leveraging digital innovations, particularly AI, to revolutionize PR/comms strategies and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission: Two-page summary detailing AI-driven technologies, specific tools used, examples of successful implementation and measurable enhancements to visibility, engagement, efficiencies and overall PR performance; two brief case studies (≤500 words each) or current Anvil submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical — One-Page Summary requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise one-page PDF summary (no longer than one page) is the single-most important component of a Bronze Anvil Tactical Award entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary should include measurable objectives, target audiences, budget and other specific information requested for the category. Results (qualitative/quantitative) must evidence how objectives were met and how the entry impacted a broader/ongoing program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze — Judging criteria (four key areas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anvil Judges evaluate Bronze entries on planning/content, creativity/quality, technical excellence, and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media relations categories are not judged on technical excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze category: Paid Promotions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of sponsorships, paid placements, or other marketing communications tactics that complement a broader PR strategy and generate exceptional ROI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efforts should be targeted and strategic and demonstrate a distinct purpose aligning with the goals of an overall campaign or specific desired outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze category: Media Relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactics, programs and events driven entirely by media relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit press releases, media advisories, pitch letters, requests for coverage, etc., plus the one-page summary including measurable objectives and results, including media impact. Upload or provide YouTube/Vimeo links to television or radio coverage. Media relations categories are not judged on technical excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze category: Feature Stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature articles written by a practitioner and submitted and published through their efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the text of the feature article and documentation of publication/placement. One-page summary should include target audience, measurable objectives and documented results. Articles must be written in entirety or substantively by the entrant (not merely pitched).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze category: Executive Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Positioning of an executive across earned, owned, and shared platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-page summary should include information about the executive, stated objectives, quantification of results and copies of significant placements, social posts or memos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze category: Social Media
rubrics_metrics.description: How social media was used to tell a story or connect with an audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share screenshots or links and provide detailed results focusing on engagement and conversions where applicable. Subcategories: 5A Single Channel Use, 5B Multichannel Use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze category: Influencer Marketing (tactical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactic focusing on using paid spokespeople and key leaders to increase awareness and drive brand messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details of achievements/benchmarks showing how the spokesperson met/exceeded campaign goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze category: Best Use of AI (tactical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate how AI played a pivotal role in enhancing or driving traditional tactical efforts within a campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples of tools used and results. Subcategories include Direct Audience Engagement, Media Relations, Social Media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze category: Digital Platform (owned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries where a digital platform was launched or substantially enhanced as part of communications efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain launch and marketing risk, end-user value and alignment with goals; include metrics and benchmarks. Entry can be completed by vendor or customer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze category: Data Insights (owned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of data or research to inform communications strategy and message development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how insights were acquired and applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze category: Websites (owned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a website as part of a communications or content marketing program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include screen grabs or copies of key pages, provide the URL, and explain how site met/exceeded communications benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze category: Non-Traditional Tactics (owned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovative, unconventional, creative tactics or approaches used as part of a PR program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document how the tactic specifically contributed to measurable results. Upload photographic/video representation of physical objects to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze category: Annual Reports (owned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications that report on an organization’s annual performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload a sample copy and a one-page summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze category: Blogs/Vlogs (owned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Web-based journals or blogs that communicated to a target audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-page summary should include rationale for blogging strategy, target audiences and statistics or other quantifiable measurements. Provide screen downloads and the actual site URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze category: Newsletters (owned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital or print publications designed to provide brief timely information to target audiences while supporting objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload samples of three consecutive issues plus a one-page summary including goals and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze category: Single-Issue Publications (owned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-issue publications designed for a special purpose; books and other publications not eligible in other categories enter here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload a sample copy and a one-page summary including goals and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze category: Magazines (owned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications designed to provide in-depth information about an organization or topic on a regular basis (print and/or digital).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload samples of three consecutive issues and a one-page summary including goals and results. Magazines typically differentiate from newsletters by number of pages and article length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze category: Video (owned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Produced videos to inform target audiences about events, brands, products, services, issues or organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-page summary should include usage statistics or other quantified measurement to support objectives; upload video files or links as requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze category: Branded Content (owned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of content generation to promote a particular brand that funds the content's production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload samples and a one-page summary including goals and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze category: Podcasts (owned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Audio programs used to tell stories, teach or share for internal or external audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide goals, results and listener feedback; explain platform engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze — Supporting materials note
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants will be asked to upload supporting documents and backup materials as requested in each category (PDFs, videos, audio, links, URLs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow individual category instructions for what to upload; ensure materials back up claims in the one-page summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific requirement — Media Relations submission components
rubrics_metrics.description: Media Relations entries should submit press releases, media advisories, pitch letters, requests for coverage, plus a one-page summary and media impact metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload broadcast coverage via YouTube/Vimeo links when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature Stories authorship requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature articles must be written in their entirety or substantively by the entrant (not merely pitched).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide text and proof of publication/placement and a one-page summary with objectives/results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational/Agency supporting artifacts (case studies, lists, letters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific organizational awards require additional artifacts like case studies, client lists, letters of recommendation, number of employees, budgets/revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Best In-House requires two brief case studies (≤500 words each) and number of employees and PR budget; Best Agency requires client list PDF with tenure; Best Solution Provider needs two letters of recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best College/University program prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for Best College/University Communications Program/Department, the college/university must have a PRSSA chapter and hold a CEPR certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include metrics on admissions, graduation, employment, internship placement, faculty counts and PRSA involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Files format and presentation requirements repeated
rubrics_metrics.description: All uploaded supporting documents must be PDFs with page size limits and minimum font/margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pages no larger than 8.5 x 11 inches (A4 for international). Minimum 10-point typeface and one-inch margins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline and fee structure (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different entry types (Silver Strategic, Silver Organizational, Bronze Tactical) have PRSA member and non-member early/regular/final deadlines and associated fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the fee table for exact early/regular/final deadlines and fees by entry type and membership status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice: Use past winning case studies as benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants are encouraged to access PRSA's database of Anvil Award-winning case studies to benchmark entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Currently only Silver Anvil Strategic case studies are available online via the provided search link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance: Include measurable objectives and metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Across categories, summaries should include measurable objectives, target audiences, budgets and documented results (qualitative and/or quantitative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges look for how results compare to objectives and how results reflect strategy/planning.
